The key classes involved here seem to be org.apache.commons.cli2.Parser, org.apache.commons.cli2.option.GroupImpl, org.apache.commons.cli2.option.OptionImpl, and the argument class which appears to have multiple implementations.

From the test:
- Option "b" is setup to require a minimum of 2 arguments and up to a maximum of 4 arguments.
- It has three default values: "100", "1000", and "10000".
- The input args are "-b", "1", "2". So only 2 arguments are passed in.
- The assertion expects the final values for option "b" to be "[1, 2, 10000]", meaning it expects the two passed arguments to be taken and the last default argument (10000) to be appended.

From the current bug report:
- The issue is that defaults only work if no arguments are passed in. It is counter-intuitive that if some arguments are passed but fewer than the max allowed, the defaults are not appended.

From Parser.parse(String[]):
- It creates a mutable list of arguments.
- It creates a new WriteableCommandLine instance with the given group and argument list.
- It calls group.defaults(commandLine) to set any defaults for the command line before processing the true input args.
- Then it processes options by iterating through the argument list.
- Finally it validates the command line.

From GroupImpl.defaults(WriteableCommandLine):
- It calls super.defaults on command line.
- Then iterates through all options in the group and calls their defaults(commandLine) method.

From OptionImpl.defaults(WriteableCommandLine):
- It does nothing in the default implementation.

This means setting defaults happens before arguments are processed.

The key flaw likely lies in:
- Argument defaults are applied only before any arguments have been processed (called from group.defaults()).
- Once arguments are processed, the command line now contains some arguments for the option.
- There is no logic to append default values if fewer than the max number of arguments are provided.
- Hence, defaults are only appended if no arguments are provided.

This reasoning explains why if an option is configured to have min=2 and max=4 args with 3 defaults, and 2 args are passed, the defaults are not appended but the assertion expects them to be.

Conclusion: The bug arises because the logic inserting default argument values is only applied when no arguments have been provided. It should be enhanced to also insert default values if fewer than maximum expected args are present, i.e. to fill out missing arguments up to minimum or maximum constraints with defaults.
